findings.summary: Staff outside the engagement teams appear only where a two-mention floor put them: the Senior Advisor, Director of Operations and Office Manager are named together in the February 2017 Barrera kickoff and the March 2017 overview and almost nowhere else in eight years, and the standing roles those documents give them (and the one a 2023 kickoff gives Julie Bailey) leave no trace in any later document.
findings.evidence: d:0003 is the only one of six kickoff memos with operations staff on the To line, and its role table gives Christopher Walton 'Edits the platform and core materials for how they will read to a reporter. Last edit before Julie Hill's review.' and Lisa Flores 'please open the billing record'. The rest of the Barrera file never shows him: the deck's 'Who is working on this' (d:0009) lists Valenzuela, Hill, Rose and Frank, and the status report says only 'Julie Hill reviewed it before it went to you' (d:0015). The 2017 overview (d:0007) profiles Walton, Flores and 'Pamela Rojas, Office Manager' but not Michael Morris, the firm's other Partner, who later sits on three of the six engagements. Outside these two documents Walton is named nowhere but his own two mundane emails, Flores only as a reporting line in d:0028, Rojas only as the addressee of one room booking (d:0019), and Walton sits on no engagement team at all. Same shape in 2023: d:0063 makes 'Consistency and style ... Lead: Julie Bailey' and asks her to set up the folder and style sheet, then she is absent from the minutes (d:0072) and from 'Engagement team: Michael Morris, Partner; Amy Carter, Communications Associate; John Macias, Associate' (d:0073). Each of these people has exactly the recipe's min_mentions_per_person of 2 planned mentions.

findings.summary: On five of six engagements the Managing Partner or Partner takes the minutes while associates and analysts sit in the room, and the junior lead writes the kickoff memo and the client status report even where the engagement letter says the senior leads the work, so who does what runs upside down.
findings.evidence: 'Julie Hill chaired the session and kept these minutes' (d:0014, with an Advisor and an Associate present); 'Minutes recorded by Julie Hill' (d:0041) and 'with Julie Hill in the chair and recording' (d:0044) on the matter whose letter says 'I will lead the engagement' (d:0038), while the kickoff for it is from Amy Carter, a Communications Associate, closing 'Thank you both for such a quick start' to the Managing Partner (d:0039); 'Notes taken by Michael Morris' with a Senior Associate and two Analysts attending (d:0055); d:0085 also authored by Julie Hill. On Suarez-Jones the letter says 'Michael Morris, a Partner of the firm, will lead the work from day to day' (d:0061), yet the kickoff is 'From: John Macias' (d:0063), the status report is 'Prepared by: John Macias, Associate' (d:0073), and the minutes end 'Corrections to these minutes should come to Michael Morris' (d:0072). The one engagement where the Partner is the ledger lead reads naturally: 'Notes taken by Michelle Black', the analyst (d:0023). Mechanism, for the fix: the M17d oversight pass appends the senior last in internal_participants, and the minutes rule (author_role 'junior') takes the last team member.

findings.summary: The engagement mail is a two-person relay addressed to a client who never writes: none of the 34 authored engagement emails is from a client, every eight-message thread alternates strictly between the same two Ashcombe senders, and the approvals the threads exist to record happen off the thread.
findings.evidence: From headers across the share: Valenzuela/Hill, Bradley/Morris, Macias/Morris and Rose/Hill alternate message by message; no external address appears in any From. Message 2 of every thread is the senior adding to the opener before the client could answer: 'One addition to Daniel's list, if I may' (d:0005), 'Building on Laura's note' (d:0048), 'I want to add one point to John's note' (d:0065), 'One addition to Michelle's note' (d:0078). The opener promises 'status, questions, and approvals for the Kirby-Taylor media work all sit in one place' (d:0047), but the approval arrives unseen: 'Thank you for approving the backgrounder, the fact sheet, and the reporter list' (d:0050), 'Your edit to the closing paragraph is in' (d:0083). Each reply quotes only the colleague's previous note. The third team member on each thread (Rose; Le and Zimmerman; Carter; Le) is copied on all eight messages and sends none.

findings.summary: Every client is exactly one person, drawn from an operations and finance title pool, who is the sole approver of everything; in a corporate communications and IR practice no client ever has a named head of communications, IR officer, CEO or counsel, and the second contacts the graph holds for two of those clients never appear.
findings.evidence: Client leads: Director of Operations (Barrera, Lee Rice, Kirby-Taylor), COO (Castaneda), VP Finance (Suarez-Jones, Gallegos). 'Mary Frank, Director of Operations ... approves drafts on the company's behalf' for a corporate positioning (d:0003); 'your confirmation that Kirby-Taylor pitches come to you alone for sign-off' to a Director of Operations on a media relations program (d:0049); 'Lauren Heath, the Chief Operating Officer, as our sponsor and the single route through which every approval will pass' (d:0020). The prose reaches for people the graph lacks and leaves them unnamed: 'your communications lead will collect comments on each draft' (d:0015) though the deck has comments 'gathered by Mary Frank' (d:0009); 'the CEO and CFO talking points' (d:0071). foundation.json holds Deborah Martin (CFO, Barrera Group) and Michael Bridges (VP Finance, Castaneda, Adams and Davis); neither is named in any document, though 'Mary Frank will confirm which operating figures the company is prepared to cite publicly' (d:0014) and the Castaneda program turns on results scripts and margin language. Every set of minutes lists the Ashcombe team plus that single contact.

findings.summary: Office mail is sent by whoever was drawn rather than by the people who hold the function: neither the Director of Operations nor Pamela Rojas, Office Manager throughout, sends any of the eight internal emails, and an Associate polices his Partner's timesheet.
findings.evidence: d:0037, John Macias (Associate) to Michael Morris (Partner): 'I checked the system before submitting my own, and yours are the two still open for the advisory group ... Michael, yours just needs Wednesday filled in', offering to enter the Partner's hours himself. The Managing Partner handles the IT provider's maintenance window ('so that we can ask the provider to work around it', d:0033) although d:0007 says Lisa Flores is responsible 'for the systems that allow a small firm to keep its commitments', and issues the conference-room booking rule (d:0016) though Pamela Rojas holds the bookings ('Pamela, the Tuesday afternoon room booking held in my name can be released', d:0019). The Client Coordinator reissues building access cards with an Office Manager in post (d:0030). Lisa Flores appears in no email header anywhere in the share.

findings.summary: The Leadership Team distribution list has one member, the Managing Partner, because lists are cut one per department; the firm's other Partner and its Director of Operations, who reports to her, are outside it.
findings.evidence: ledger/distribution_lists.json: {"id": "dl:leadership", "name": "Leadership Team", "address": "leadership@ashcombeadvisory.com", "members": ["p:julie.hill"]}. Michael Morris (Partner) is only on advisory@, Lisa Flores (Director of Operations, reports_to p:julie.hill) only on all-staff@.

findings.summary: The graph keeps the departed Communications Analyst employed: her works_at edge never closes, while the roster ends her employment in 2020 and the ACL and distribution lists treat her as gone.
findings.evidence: foundation.json p:michelle.black 'employment': {'start': '2015-09-26', 'end': '2020-07-08'}; acl.json grant for p:michelle.black has 'docs': []; she is on neither all-staff@ nor advisory@. ledger/graph.json and evals/graph_expected.json both carry {"src": "p:michelle.black", "dst": "x:ashcombe-advisory", "kind": "works_at", "start": "2015-09-26", "end": null}. fabric/graph.py never sets an end on an internal works_at edge, so this is generator-level.

findings.summary: The ACL half of this dimension carries no signal on this org: the open posture gives all 15 current staff the identical 104-document grant and the departed analyst none, which is a common real small-firm setup but sits beside engagement letters that promise need-to-know access.
findings.evidence: acl.json: every current person's grant is the same 104 paths, including Finance/ and People/ and the crisis and investor relations folders; p:michelle.black has 'docs': []. The letters say 'limit access to those members of our team who need it' (d:0018) and 'disclose it only to Firm personnel who require it for that work' (d:0038). No defect claimed: the recipe declares acl_posture open and flat shares with need-to-know boilerplate are ordinary; a partitioning posture is needed to test who-can-read-what here.
